proposals.subject: Muusoctopus sp.
proposals.title: I meant that to stay inside
proposals.body:
The light came closer. I kept my arms folded in front of me and tried to look as though I had been busy.

Went red instead.

I could feel myself going pale before I had decided what to do about the red.

Uncurled one arm. Then another. Whoever it was had waited through both, and I still wanted a closer look.

media.sourceCaption: A stare down with this octopus (Mussoctopus sp.), occurred during Dive 08 of the Seascape Alaska 5 expedition. As we observed it, the octopus displayed its abilities to change color using specialized cells in its skin called chromatophores. It flashed the deep reddish purple seen here before turning completely white within seconds.

Source caption misspells genus Mussoctopus; retain literal source caption while canonical taxon remains Muusoctopus. No species-level identification invented.
proposals.chronology: Propose after The arms underneath. This develops curiosity after a defensive-looking first response without erasing that prior passage. No egg, mating or terminal event added. Gilda’s brood is unaffected.
proposals.fictionBoundary: NOAA explicitly records a stare-down and red-purple followed by white within seconds. The still documents the red-purple phase, eyes and foreground arms. Approaching light, feigned busyness, awareness and emotional meaning of color, arm timing and desire for a closer look are fictional. No claim that this genus blushes from embarrassment or that source observers diagnosed her emotions.
proposals.distinctness: Current admitted Elspeth passage divides arms between display and holding ground. This new passage concerns failed concealment of interest and the decision to approach after an observer remains through a visible change. It avoids a new threat, rescue or small-animal protection. Lead must judge whether this remains too close in emotional movement.

At a depth of 1,650 meters (5,414 feet), during the seventh dive of the 2023 Shakedown + EXPRESS West Coast Exploration expedition, we came upon this deep-sea octopus in the genus Muusoctopus. It didn’t seem too bothered or impressed by the presence of remotely operated vehicle Deep Discoverer, but if you look closely at the seafloor around it, you’ll notice several brittle stars who had other ideas and are on the move!

sourceReviews.sourceCaption: Adult female California sea lion nursing her newborn pup at San Miguel Island, California. The brand on her left shoulder is a permanent brand that identifies her for survival and reproductive rate studies. Marine conditions since 2012 have illustrated that. An unusual marine heat wave off the West Coast known as “the blob” combined with an El Niño climate pattern reduced pup production and survival , with thousands of malnourished pups stranding on Southern California beaches. NOAA Fisheries declared the elevated number of deaths an Unusual Mortality Event in 2013 . The first sighting in the water is usually of the round head. The fore flippers are small and placed far forward with five long, clawed digits. The longer hind flippers are used for locomotion under water but cannot be turned forward as with sea lions. Harbor seals wriggle and hunch to travel on land. sourceReviews.sourceCaption: Common bottlenose dolphin in Biscayne Bay, Florida with debris. Credit: NOAA Fisheries/Jesse Wicker (Permit #779-1633) Marine debris is any human-made material that ends up in our waterways like microplastics, soda cans, plastic bags, larger discarded items, and more. Marine mammals can become entangled in some of these items like discarded ropes, fabric, or plastic which can become embedded in the animal’s skin as it grows. In addition, animals often ingest discarded plastic items and bags, which can lead to serious internal injury—like tearing the digestive tract—and causing blockages. preservedHeldPassage.title: A little less octopus
preservedHeldPassage.body: The brittle stars scattered when I came round the stone. I stopped, pulled my arms closer, and waited. One came back. I am trying very hard not to reach for it.
preservedHeldPassage.status: Still held and unchanged in source file; reproduced here only to make repetition check explicit.
